lines.en: I tap on Karin’s name in my phone and wait for her to answer.
It’s that weird part of the afternoon between lunch and dinner where I want to eat, but having four meals in one day is kind of frowned upon.
But I’m sure if I told Karin that, she wouldn’t mind.
Maybe the two of us could go out for lunch or something?
That sounds like a thing she’d enjoy.
Sure, she’ll probably drop her phone when I ask, but I think she’d enjoy it when all is said and done.
: Hello! I mean...hi!
: Hey!
: All three of those mean the exact same thing, Karin. Any of them will work in the future.
: Okay but “hello” is too formal and “hi” is too informal and if I accidentally added an extra y to “hey” you would have thought I was too clingy.
: Are these things that girls actually think of?
: Greetings! H...How are you today?!
: Hungry.
: Do you...
: Do you want me to make you lunch?
: Or...dinner, I guess?
: It's that weird part of the day between the two, so I don’t really know what to call it.
: I was actually wondering if you’d maybe want to go out to a diner or something?
: Ah! D-Diner?!
A loud bang rings out through my cell-phone, signaling that Karin has, just as I expected, dropped the phone upon being asked out.
She’s so pure.
: S-Sorry! My hand slipped!
: I had a lot of coffee today and...um...hands.
: Right...
: So, what do you say?
: I’d love to!
: Great, then-
: But...
: Uh-oh.
: My parents are expecting a package and they asked me if I could sign for it when it gets here.
: Can’t Kirin do it instead?
: I..don’t know where she is.
: But, umm...
: Maybe if...
: If you wanted to...come over?
: I...I wasn’t really joking when I offered to make you lunch...or dinner.
: Which one did we decide this was again?
: I don’t think we did.
: But if that’s really okay, I’ll start heading over now.
: Okay! Yeah! I’ll...um...
: I’m gonna take a shower and get dressed then.
: You...you know where I live, right?
: Yeah. I’ve met Kirin there before.
: Right...right. Yeah. Okay!
: Umm...just...call me when you get here, then!
: I’ll see you soon!
The two of us hang up and I begin to make my way over to the Kanda residence.
It will be the first time I’m hanging out with Karin alone in the apartment, and I fully expect it to be disastrous in the cutest possible way.
Karin lets me in after I text her about my arrival. And, before I know it, we’re awkwardly standing in the living room, staring at each other.
: So...umm...did you find the place okay?
: Yup. Didn’t I just tell you earlier that I remembered where you live?
: Y-Yeah...but my mom always talks about how boys can be forgetful, so...I thought maybe you’d...you know...forget.
: She could just be saying all of that to justify how my dad forgot their anniversary this year, though.
: Well, it’s true that my memory is probably one of the worst you’ll ever find, but it’s for reasons entirely unrelated to anniversaries and whatnot.
: What’s...what’s wrong with your memory? Is it okay for me to ask that?
: Let’s just say a lot of it disappeared.
: And I guess the rest of it could technically disappear again...but only at several really specific moments.
: Like when seasons change or something.
: I don’t really understand how it works, to tell you the truth.
: Is that...some sort of...disease?
: No, it’s more like-
: I...I’ll take care of you!
: You don’t need to worry, Sensei!
: I’ll wait by your bedside every morning and show you flashcards to remind you of who I am! And who everyone else is!
: You don’t have to worry! Everything will be okay!
: I appreciate the offer, but I’m pretty sure I’ll be fine.
: Please continue to spend your mornings working out or whatever else it is that you do.
: I...watch the news sometimes?
: While you’re working out, I’m guessing?
: ...Maybe.
: Well, in the event that my memory does randomly disappear again, I’d love for you to come remind me of who I am.
: You’ll probably have to fight off a small girl with red hair who will be attempting to do the same exact thing, though.
: But I don’t want to fight Ami...she’s so nice.
: Maybe we can just take turns?
: Or I can just...cook for you while she reads you the flashcards.
: I still want to make them, though. I have this weird thing where I just really like flashcards for some reason.
: Do you want to talk more about flashcards? That sounds fun, right?
: It sounds...like a thing.
: I’m more interested in the part about you cooking.
: Oh! Right! That’s why you’re here!
: Look! Table!
I “Look. Table.” to find that Karin has laid out two surprisingly large sushi platters.
And when I say “surprisingly large” I mean both the platters and the actual pieces of sushi are gigantic.
I was all about the idea of a fourth meal today, but...this might be a little too much.
: So, umm...I’m sorry for not asking you what you wanted.
: If you hate it, we can just order from somewhere.
: Actually, let’s just do that right now. This clearly isn’t good enough for you.
: I’m sure it’s fine, Karin.
: Oh! And...umm...I didn’t know what you would want to drink, so I just got you...one of everything we had.
: Is that canned coffee?
: Yes!
: Do you normally drink canned coffee with sushi?
: No!
: Oh God...I’ve ruined everything.
: I’m so sorry, Sensei. I’ll just get my phone and-
: It's fine, Karin. There’s no reason to order takeout when you’ve already done this much.
: I’m not drinking the canned coffee, though.
: I’m no gourmet, but that doesn’t sound like it would be a good flavor combination.
: Are you sure you don’t want a pizza or something?
: I want to eat what you made.
: Are you sure?
: Of course.
: But what if I’m not good enough?
: Or...the food! I meant the food! What if the food isn’t good enough?
: You’ll never want to come over again and I’ll be too embarrassed to look at you during practice!
: Then I’ll have to quit the soccer team and start pursuing another sport full time and it will destroy my future and I’ll lose any scholarship I could have gotten and...
: And before I know it I’ll wind up severely injuring myself and never being able to play anything ever again!
: I’m not sure how you got to the last part, but I think it might be time for us to sit down and eat.
: Okay! But please...please stop me if I start rambling again! I mean it!
: Sure...
Karin and I move to our respective spots at the table.
I take my place behind a plethora of beverages that she was apparently torn between-
And she takes her place behind...
: Is...is something wrong?
: Is that a glass of wine?
: Wine?...
: That’s a glass of wine.
: I’m not old enough to drink this.
: You're not secretly an alcoholic, are you?
: What?! No! I must have poured it by mistake when I was pouring yours!
: I’m only allowed to drink on special occasions!
: Is today not a special occasion?
: It is! But...it’s a different kind of special!
: It has to be a holiday!
: I kind of want to see you drink now.
: Wh...why would you want to see that?
: Just curious about how much it changes your personality.
: Who knows? Maybe you’re a lot more relaxed with alcohol in your system?
: Please don’t say things that will lead to me having a drinking problem...
: If I find out wine is the key to holding a conversation with you, I’ll be sneaking bottles into[school] before I know it.
: This conversation never happened.
: But...um...
: I...I wouldn’t mind if you...maybe came over for a holiday sometime...if you really wanted to see.
: I can’t drink a lot but...it would make me happy having you around for something like that...
: I’m sure it would. I can’t imagine your parents would feel the same way, though.
: Oh.
: Right.
: I have parents.
: Parents who I imagine wouldn’t be very fond of their daughter dating a staff member at the[school].
: Yeah...they-
: Wait...
: Are...
: Are you saying you would...date me?
Shit.
I guess I did kind of say that.
It’s definitely not what I meant, though.
I mean, a relationship with Karin does sound like it would be...surprisingly normal-
But a relationship in general isn’t something that I want.
Or at least it’s not something I think I want.
I don’t know.
Maybe in a different life.
As far as this one goes, though-
: I’m sorry. I didn’t mean it like that.
: Ah, no! You don’t have to apologize! I wasn’t trying to put you on the spot!
: It just sounded like...you might...l-like me or something...that’s all...
: I mean, obviously you wouldn’t like someone like me. I don’t even know what kind of drinks you prefer with sushi.
: That’s actually the first thing I quiz my prospective girlfriends on.
: Hmm...
: What’s that face for?
: I’m waiting to see which one you drink first in case this ever happens again.
: Also, what other types of questions are on this quiz?
: Look at you getting all serious in the face of romance.
: Oh my God! I did it! I flirted with a boy!
: I'm not sure if I'd count something that small as flirting, but at least it was smooth.
: At least a lot smoother than openly celebrating your success.
: I’m a boy expert now.
: You haven’t been sneaking sips of that wine while I’m not looking, have you?
: Of course not...
: But I’m...finally starting to calm down, I think.
: My heart’s still beating out of my chest, but...I think that “dating” thing gave me a temporary boost to my self-esteem.
: Even though I immediately said I didn’t mean anything by it?
: Weird, right? Maybe that part just hasn’t settled in yet?
: Or maybe I’m just finally-
: Wait. No. It’s here.
: I’m going to die alone with ten cats.
: No one is truly alone with ten cats.
: Do you like cats, Sensei?!
: Not really.
: Oh.
: But...their ears.
: And their little noses...
: I just meant that all human beings are inherently alone as a matter of principle, so the only way to properly judge loneliness is by sheer tangibility.
: If there are ten other living creatures in the same room as you, whether they be cats or humans, you are not technically alone.
: But you are still alone.
: Get it?
: But...their ears...
: And their little noses...
: Let’s just eat now...
I decide to stop being depressing for a moment and enjoy the food Karin prepared for us.
I’m surprised she was able to make something as classy as a sushi platter with virtually no mistakes whatsoever.
I’m not even sure if Ami can make sushi at this level, and she’s pretty much a personal chef at this point.
I guess if anyone was going to be able to, though, it was Karin.
Despite her tomboyish hobbies and a physique that would make even professional athletes jealous, she’s a pure, wholesome girl at heart.
A wholesome girl who wants to make the people around her happy, and who wants to find happiness of her own without damaging anyone else in the process.
I wish her luck in that regard.
Personally, I don’t think something like that is possible.
But I’d be happy to be proven wrong.
Karin’s affection has increased to [karin_love]!
Thirty minutes later...I leave Karin’s house and decide to get on with my day...
